issues.description: validate_conda contract under-specifies the postcondition: substring match on '--version' output accepts impostors.
issues.detail: The contract should be: 'returns True iff the path is an executable that identifies itself as conda/mamba/micromamba'. The implementation checks substring containment in lowercased output, so any binary whose --version output contains the substring 'conda' (e.g. 'anaconda-uninstall', 'conda-build') satisfies it. Tighten the postcondition: require the tool name as the first token, or parse a known version format.

issues.description: validate_conda violates its own contract for the empty-string precondition by returning True ('valid').
issues.detail: Returning True for an empty path conflates 'no input supplied' with 'valid executable'. This is an LSP-style postcondition weakening: callers expecting 'True implies executable is usable' get a false positive. Either split the contract (is_empty vs is_valid) or treat empty as a precondition violation and skip validation at the call site instead.

issues.description: Filter '*.exe' leaks Windows implementation through a cross-platform abstraction.
issues.detail: The file-browser filter restricts selection to '*.exe', which excludes valid Unix conda executables (no extension) and shell wrappers. The abstraction 'Conda executable path' should be platform-neutral; the dialog filter leaks a Windows-only assumption through the interface. Use platform-conditional filters or 'All files'.

issues.description: kernelspec argv() silently ignores an invalid custom conda_path when the checkbox is on.
issues.detail: When custom_conda is True, the code reads conda_path and uses it without re-validating; only if it is falsy does the error path fire. A user-set path that fails validate_conda at config time can still be persisted (validation only blocks on edit), and a stale/broken path will be passed downstream. Re-check on use and surface a precise error pointing at the preference.

issues.description: create_browsefile signature extension is fine, but the contract for validate_callback is undocumented.
issues.detail: The new parameters validate_callback / validate_reason are added without a docstring stating the callback's contract (signature, return semantics, when invoked, threading). Future implementers will inherit this widget and likely violate the unspecified contract. Add a short spec at the method docstring so subtypes and callers share the same expectations.

issues.description: conda_path option lives under 'main_interpreter' but is consumed by ipythonconsole; module boundary is muddy.
issues.detail: The setting is logically about kernel activation, but is stored in the interpreter section and consumed from kernelspec via get_conf with a hard-coded section string. That cross-module coupling should be mediated by a small accessor (e.g. get_custom_conda_executable()) so the section name is an implementation detail of one module, not a fact every caller must know.

review.summary: The PR extends a reasonable abstraction — 'where do we find conda' — with a user-supplied override, but the contract for the new validate_conda function is loose: empty input returns True, and the identity check is a lowercase substring scan that admits impostors. A leaky '*.exe' filter ties the cross-platform 'Conda executable' abstraction to Windows. The conda_path option also crosses a module boundary (stored under main_interpreter, consumed by ipythonconsole) without a thin accessor, and the kernelspec consumer trusts the persisted value without re-validation. Tighten the validate_conda postcondition, document the new browsefile callback contract, and route the cross-plugin read through a named accessor.
